capability_investigated:
generate(features, prompts, ...) signature and the WhisperFeatureExtractor
output shape — specifically whether the decode call accepts a batched
StorageView (N x n_mels x 3000) with a parallel prompt list rather than a
single 30s window.
what_i_learned:
The processor pads/truncates every input to a fixed 30s mel window, so the
stub silently dropped everything past the first 30 seconds of each call
(pure deletion). generate takes a list of prompts, so a batched feature
StorageView with one prompt per window decodes all segments in a single
call and returns one result per window.
hypothesis:
Split audio into ceil(len/30s) non-overlapping 30s windows, extract all
features at once, run one batched generate over [prompt]*N, and join the
per-window transcripts. This recovers the deleted tail and should sharply
raise length_ratio.p05 / cut the deletion rate that dominates the stub.

capability_investigated:
Re-examined generate()'s memory behavior on a batched StorageView: how peak
GPU allocation scales with the number of 30s windows passed in one decode
call (N x n_mels x 3000 features + N parallel beams).
what_i_learned:
generate() decodes all prompts in the list concurrently, so a single batched
call over every window of a long call allocates memory proportional to the
window count — long 0715 calls have enough windows to exceed GPU memory
(CUDA out of memory). Decoding one window per generate() call bounds peak
memory to a single 30s window and still recovers the full tail.
hypothesis:
Keep the long-form windowing that fixed the tail-deletion, but iterate the
windows through generate() one at a time instead of one giant batched call;
this removes the OOM crash while preserving the deletion fix, so the
iteration actually scores.

capability_investigated:
The WhisperGenerationResult object returned by frozen.generate() — specifically
its scores and no_speech_prob fields, and the return_scores /
return_no_speech_prob decode flags that populate them. Also the n-gram
blocking knob no_repeat_ngram_size on the decode call.
what_i_learned:
generate() exposes per-sequence avg log-prob (scores) and a per-window
no_speech_prob, but ONLY when return_scores=True / return_no_speech_prob=True
are passed — otherwise result.scores is empty and the signals are discarded.
This means coverage loss can be localized: every window IS decoded (loss isn't
at the chunker), so low length_ratio comes from individual windows collapsing
into repetition / early-EOS, detectable via low score + low unique-token ratio
while no_speech_prob stays low.
hypothesis:
Condition a fallback on those discarded signals: greedy-decode each window,
and only when its output is empty / score < -1.0 / repetitive AND
no_speech_prob < 0.6 (real speech present) re-decode once with beam_size=5 +
no_repeat_ngram_size=3 to break the loop and recover the deleted span. Targets
the dominant deletion axis without touching windows that already decode clean.
